record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.context_brief: Reduction-based creative telescoping for mixed terms
record.original_question: Develop a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm for a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term f_n(x) in the summation setting. The algorithm should compute, when possible, rational functions c_0(x), c_1(x), ..., c_r(x) in C(x), not all zero, together with a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term g_n(x), such that c_0 f_n(x) + c_1 D_x f_n(x) + ... + c_r D_x^r f_n(x) = g_{n+1}(x) - g_n(x).

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1 Develop a reduction based creative telescoping algorithm which for a given hypergeometric-hyperexponential term fn(x) computes, if possible, rational functions c0, c1, ··· , cr in C(x), not all zero, such that there exists a hypergeometric-hyperexponential term gn(x) with c0fn(x) + c1Dxfn(x) + ··· + crDr_xfn(x) = gn+1(x) − gn(x).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $x, n$ be independent indeterminates. A bivariate term $f_n(x)$ is called hypergeometric–hyperexponential over $C(x,n)$ if both the shift quotient $f_{n+1}(x)/f_n(x)$ and the logarithmic derivative $(D_x f_n(x))/f_n(x)$ lie in $C(x,n)$, where $D_x$ denotes differentiation with respect to $x$ and the shift $n \mapsto n+1$ acts on $n$.

Design a reduction-based creative telescoping algorithm in the summation setting that, given such a hypergeometric–hyperexponential term $f_n(x)$, decides whether there exist a nonnegative integer $r$, rational functions $c_0(x), c_1(x), \dots, c_r(x) \in C(x)$ not all zero, and a hypergeometric–hyperexponential term $g_n(x)$ such that
$$c_0(x)\, f_n(x) + c_1(x)\, D_x f_n(x) + \cdots + c_r(x)\, D_x^{\,r} f_n(x) \;=\; g_{n+1}(x) - g_n(x),$$
and that computes such $c_0,\dots,c_r$ and $g_n$ when they exist. The algorithm should be "reduction-based" in the sense that the telescoper $L = \sum_i c_i(x) D_x^i$ is obtained from a Hermite/Abramov–Petkovšek-style reduction of the shift class of $f_n(x)$ rather than by computing a certificate directly.
artifact.status_search_result: Reduction-based creative telescoping for mixed hypergeometric–hyperexponential terms has been developed in the integration setting (Bostan–Dumont–Salvy, ISSAC 2016) and reduction-based methods have separately been developed for pure hypergeometric summation and, recently, for definite summation of D-finite functions and a unified hypergeometric/q-hypergeometric reduction. We did not find a published paper specifically presenting a reduction-based algorithm for the summation setting on mixed hypergeometric–hyperexponential terms with telescoper in $D_x$ as posed; status is unclear from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Algorithms for Mixed Creative Telescoping
status_evidence.snippet: Creative telescoping algorithm focusing on the integration of bivariate hypergeometric-hyperexponential terms, based on a Hermite-like reduction procedure.
status_evidence.claim: Solves the integration (not summation) variant for mixed hypergeometric-hyperexponential terms.

status_evidence.title: Reduction-based creative telescoping for definite summation of D-finite functions
status_evidence.snippet: Reduction-based creative telescoping for definite summation of D-finite functions.
status_evidence.claim: Reduction-based summation algorithms exist for D-finite functions, a related but distinct class.

status_evidence.title: A unified reduction for hypergeometric and q-hypergeometric creative telescoping
status_evidence.snippet: A unified reduction algorithm applicable to both hypergeometric terms and their q-analogues.
status_evidence.claim: Unified reduction in summation for hypergeometric and q-hypergeometric, not specifically the mixed continuous-discrete summation problem.
